_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-14 · Sky153 — the military side is scoped, and it is not what we expected.
_status: The military side of the credit recommendations is now measured. It is 98% of everything in the dataset, and the surprise is that it is far TIDIER than the college-typed side, not messier — the American Council on Education publishes each recommendation and MAP stores it, so 93% of them already carry one single agreed wording. A third of that vocabulary can be cleaned up with no human judgement at all, against about a tenth on the college-typed side. The catch is size and naming: there are three times as many distinct topics, the work is much more spread out (about 250 decisions to cover half of it rather than 50), and almost none of them can be named from an official course number, because ACE recommends subject areas like 'Supervision' rather than courses. One real discovery: Marine Corps records have rank abbreviations baked into the recommendation text itself, which split 482 topics that are really the same thing. Separately, Sam asked whether Sierra knows about the required-evidence field in MAP — she does not, and we have never even asked MAP for it; a probe is running to find out whether that field is cut short at the source or just in the viewer.

items.text: The required-evidence text is NOT cut short at the source — longest value is 349 characters and lengths vary freely, so what looked truncated in your JSON view is the viewer. It is now being fetched daily, along with the submission guidelines field, which is arguably the more useful of the two ("must submit MJC CPL Petition Form"). One thing to know before we show it to students: it is blank on military records by design — every welding and MOS row we sampled had it empty — so Sierra must never say "no evidence required" for a military exhibit. Decision needed: publish it to Sierra?

One decision that changes a fifth of the military work. The same ACE exhibit sometimes recommends the same topic at 1, 2 and 3 hours — for example Orienteering. Are those one recommendation with a range of hours, or genuinely different ones? We already ruled that hours are not part of a recommendation's identity, but that ruling came from colleges writing the same course differently, which is not quite this situation.

How finely should military subject areas be split? ACE lists Supervision, Principles of Supervision and Introduction to Supervision separately. One reference or three? Your answer sets the size of the whole military job. Warning from the data: do not extend this to Management — it looks similar but Project Management and Supply Chain Management are genuinely different subjects, not variations.

Build the mechanical clean-up for the military lane before any worklist — it is worth a third here, against a tenth on the college side. Four steps: the not-a-topic rows, pure capitalisation differences, hours as an attribute, and stripping the Marine Corps rank abbreviations. The rank step needs its list widened first — 176 topics still do not land cleanly.

482 military topics carry a rank abbreviation inside the recommendation text, splitting things that are really one topic across 12,157 rows. Stripping the rank reunites 306 of them with a topic that already exists. This is the same Marine Corps duplication already recorded in memory, showing up in the wording rather than in the counts.

The 'questions Sierra struggled with' list should now read about 13 instead of 78 — the rest was the automated test suite that runs on every deploy. Each row can be marked Handled or Leave it, and there is a bulk control for all of them at once. Marking does not change how Sierra answers; it only clears the list.

One decision only you can make. Eight colleges still show a contact from the old June snapshot even though MAP now holds nobody for them. They keep the old name so nobody is left with a dead end — but MAP is the system of record, and a blank there might mean that person left the role. Should those eight go blank instead?

Seven fallback contacts were found by web search and the code deliberately refuses to propose them, because no session could open the pages to apply Jessica's sourcing rules. They render as 'Candidate — confirm' and still need a human or a differently-connected pass.

Still open from an earlier session: a site phrase currently opens its own tabs plus every shared CPL tab. That is only safe while everyone holding one is trusted with all shared CPL data. Worth deciding before the Finance phrase reaches anyone in Finance.

The Common CR Reference tab is live — a new tab beside the Common Course/Subjects/Exhibit References. Please work the top of the list (it is ranked so the most valuable decision is always first) and confirm or reject the groupings. The top 50 wordings account for about half of every articulation in the system, so this is an afternoon, not an ocean.

Inside that tab, 38 groups are badged with an orange 'AJ 110? — check'. Those are cases where an official C-ID title says something completely different from what every college wrote. We deliberately did NOT apply the official name — one of them would have renamed 'Physical Training and Health Education' to 'Introduction to Criminal Justice'. Tell us if we are being too cautious.

A free win: 3,242 rows say '0 hours in Credit Is Not Recommended' and 2,269 say 'Credit may be granted on the basis of an individualized assessment'. Neither is a credit recommendation at all. They belong in the 'not a topic' bucket and are the same population we already flagged as an automatic Not-Applicable win.
